newsitem.title: FRANCE: SWIMMING-SMITH WILL NOT COMMIT HERSELF TO SEVILLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-SMITH WILL NOT COMMIT HERSELF TO SEVILLE.

text.p: Triple Olympic champion Michelle Smith would not commit herself on Saturday to either of the next two major international championships.
"I don't know yet if I'll take part in the European championships in Seville or the worlds in Perth," Smith said after racing at the Sarcelles meeting near Paris on Saturday.
"In any case, I've already qualified. But I'm going to wait and I'll decide depending on my results. If I go to Seville I'll go to Perth," added the 26-year-old Irishwoman.
The Seville meeting is in August, Perth next January.
Smith won the 800 metres freestyle here in an Irish record eight minutes 52.10 seconds.
She was third in the 100 metres backstroke behind Roxanna Maracinealu of France, who broke the French record, and Anke Scholl of Germany.
Smith will race against Germany's Franziska van Almsick, who is making a comeback after retiring following the Atlanta Olympics, in the 100 metres freestyle on Sunday.
Racing in her speciality, the 200 metres freestyle, on Saturday, van Almsick won in two minutes 02.52 seconds, 5.74 seconds off her world record of 1:56.78.
World champion van Almsick only managed the silver medal in the 200 freestyle at the Atlanta Games.
